Then hand behind the back, note the distance between the two hands. One side after the other. Also note whether the arms touch the wall without the lower back lifting.

x.le test du genou au mur : trente seconde: the knee-to-wall test: thirty seconds, barefoot, heel down

x.Les deux mesures ne tiennent pas ensembl: The two measurements do not fit together: no ratio is calculated from them.
x.Chez l’homme de plus de 1,65 m : ossatur: For men over 1.65 m: fine bone structure under 16.5 cm of wrist, thick above 19 cm.
x.Rapport de volume quadriceps / ischios a: Quad / hamstring volume ratio above 2.0 over the last trained weeks. On the side photo: thigh developed in front, flat behind.
x.Aucune. C’est une histoire de programmat: None. It is a programming matter, not a morphology one, and that is precisely why it must be read first.
x.Leg curl sous deux profils de résistance: Leg curl under two resistance profiles (lying for the long position, seated for the short position), Romanian deadlift, hip thrust, long lunges.
x.on déplace des séries : les mêmes séance: we move sets around: the same sessions, a different split. It is the cheapest correction in the document.
x.Ramener le rapport sous 1,5 sur huit à d: Bring the ratio under 1.5 over eight to twelve weeks, and check it with the volume counter that already exists.
x.Le même raisonnement se généralise à tou: The same reasoning generalizes to all pairs: chest/back, front/rear delts, biceps/triceps, abs/lower back.
x.Expliquer des ischios plats par « la gén: Explaining flat hamstrings by “genetics” when the logbook shows two sets a week against twelve for quads. The reading order (acquired, functional, bone) exists for that.
x.Écart droite/gauche sur biceps, cuisse o: Right/left gap on biceps, thigh or calf, sustained over at least three consecutive check-ins and above measurement error. On video: sideways bar deviation, uneven support.
x.Sans objet : c’est un constat, pas une s: Not applicable: it is an observation, not a structure. And everyone has a normal asymmetry.
x.Travail unilatéral, en commençant systém: Unilateral work, always starting with the weak side and matching the strong side to its rep count, not the other way round.
x.ils ne sont pas à retirer : on ajoute de: they are not to be removed: we add unilateral work alongside, and Motion Lab is used to check the bar no longer drifts.
x.Réévaluation à trois bilans. Si l’écart: Reassess after three check-ins. If the gap does not move despite unilateral work, we stop pushing and refer to a healthcare professional if there is any discomfort.
x.Le seuil compte plus que le signal. Avec: The threshold matters more than the signal. With a technical error around a centimeter on a self-measured arm, a 1 cm gap means nothing. You need a clear, repeated gap, never an isolated one.
x.Lancer une chasse à l’asymétrie sur du b: Launching an asymmetry hunt on measurement noise. It is the surest way to make an athlete anxious about their body, and exactly what an app must never do.
x.Un squat complet demande de l’ordre de 3: A full squat needs around 35–40° of dorsiflexion. Without it, the body borrows range elsewhere. The cause is not always flexibility: it can be joint-related. The test says range is missing, not why.
x.Presse à cuisses, hack squat, extension: Leg press, hack squat, leg extension: the quads are loaded without demanding the ankle. Heel-elevated squat: the meta-analysis shows a gain in ankle and knee range from about 2.5 cm of elevation, with a dose effect.
x.cale de 2,5 cm, ou stance élargi avec po: 2.5 cm wedge, or wider stance with toes turned out
x.fentes arrière ou bulgares, qui demanden: reverse or Bulgarian lunges, which need less dorsiflexion on the front leg
x.Deux voies en parallèle : la cale pour s: Two tracks in parallel: the wedge to train today, range work to stop needing it. The app must say which of the two it is proposing: a wedge is a workaround, not a treatment.
x.La cale n’est pas gratuite : la même mét: The wedge is not free: the same meta-analysis shows that a large elevation reduces hip and trunk range. The work is shifted to the quads, not added to them. This must be stated explicitly.
x.Attribuer à la morphologie ce qui vient: Attributing to morphology what comes from the ankle. The knee-to-wall test takes thirty seconds and must be done before any conclusion about levers.
x.Flexion de hanche qui bute franchement,: Hip flexion that stops clearly, with pelvic tilt, and a firm rather than elastic stop. Often a marked asymmetry between internal and external rotation. In the squat: depth limited whatever the stance, or pinching in the groin.
x.La structure de hanche varie énormément: Hip structure varies enormously from person to person: femoral neck orientation spans about thirty degrees, and so does the socket’s. In practice, one person squats toes nearly straight and goes deep, another stops early and needs to turn out. It is not flexibility to be gained.
x.La recherche du stance, méthodiquement :: Finding the stance, methodically: width and toe angle tested in steps, at light load, noting comfortable depth. Then machines that bypass the range: leg press with high feet, hack, leg curl, extension.
x.profondeur choisie, celle où il n’y a pa: chosen depth, the one without pinching
x.ouvrir les pointes et élargir le stance: turn the toes out and widen the stance
x.prudence : il demande de la rotation ext: caution: it demands external rotation this profile may not have (test at light load before programming it)
x.Amplitude utile plutôt qu’amplitude maxi: Useful range rather than maximum range. Long-position work is sought in exercises where the hip is not the stop: lying leg curl, lunges, press.
x.Distinguer butée osseuse et raideur dema: Telling a bone stop from stiffness requires imaging no one will get. RepCore describes the test and stays silent on the cause: “the stop is firm and comes with pelvic tilt” is an observation.
x.L’amplitude manquante est empruntée à la: The missing range is borrowed from the spine or the scapula. It is not a strength flaw: it is a travel constraint.
x.Développés assis à dossier (le dossier e: Seated presses with a back pad (the pad blocks lumbar borrowing and makes it visible), dumbbells rather than barbell (the path adapts), neutral grip, cables for raises.
x.devant, ou à la machine : la trajectoire: in front, or on a machine: the path stays guided and the lower back no longer has to make up the missing range
x.devant : le dos travaille autant, et l’é: in front: the back works just as much, and the shoulder no longer has to find a rotation it doesn’t have
x.revenir vers 180 % de la largeur d’épaul: go back toward 180% of shoulder width
x.limiter la descente au point où l’épaule: limit the descent to the point where the shoulder stays in front, without chasing the bottom
x.Amplitude d’épaule travaillée à part, ho: Shoulder range worked separately, outside heavy sets, and reassessed every two months. As long as it is missing, load stays on guided paths.
x.C’est le profil le plus évolutif du docu: It is the most changeable profile in the document: an athlete flagged in January may no longer be in May. The profile therefore carries an expiry date.
x.Figer l’aménagement. Un exercice écarté: Freezing the adjustment. An exercise set aside for range reasons and never reopened becomes a permanent ban born of a thirty-second test.
x.Chaîne postérieure raide : le faux mauva: Stiff posterior chain: the false poor puller
x.Dos qui s’enroule tôt en flexion avant j: Back that rounds early in a straight-leg forward bend. In the deadlift: rounded lower back from the start, not only under fatigue.
x.Ce n’est pas un problème de levier : c’e: It is not a lever problem: it is missing range. The difference is decisive because the two answers are opposite: an unfavorable lever is bypassed with a variation, stiffness is worked on.
x.surélever la barre jusqu’à ce que le dos: raise the bar until the back holds
x.Amplitude d’abord, charge ensuite. Et un: Range first, load second. And a dated reassessment: this profile should disappear within a few months if the work is done.
x.À ne pas confondre avec un tronc long, q: Not to be confused with a long torso, which produces the same picture (a back that suffers in the deadlift) for the opposite reason. The forward-bend test tells them apart in ten seconds.
x.Fémur long, tronc court : le squatteur p: Long femur, short torso: the leaning squatter
x.Pour garder la charge au-dessus du milie: To keep the load over mid-foot, a long femur forces the pelvis back further, so the torso leans. The lean shortens the knee’s lever arm and lengthens the hip’s: at equal load, this squat taxes the hip extensors more than an upright squat. It is not a technique fault, it is the solution geometry imposes.
x.Tout ce qui découple genou et hanche (pr: Everything that decouples knee and hip (leg press, hack squat, Bulgarian squat, leg extension) because they load the quads without the torso lean. And everything that pays off the hip lever: deadlift, hinge, glutes.
x.barre basse ou squat guidé, stance élarg: low bar or guided squat, wider stance, toes turned out, 1.5 to 2.5 cm wedge
x.raccourcir le pas ou passer en bulgare: shorten the step or switch to Bulgarian
x.Quadriceps par les machines et le travai: Quads through machines and unilateral work, not through the free squat. The hinge becomes the strong lift: program it as such rather than fighting a squat that will never be their ground.
x.Lui vendre de la mobilité de cheville pe: Selling them ankle mobility for six months to “straighten” their squat. A wedge settles in one session what a long femur will never give up. Check the ankle before blaming the femur.
x.Tronc long, jambes courtes : le levier d: Long torso, short legs: the back lever
x.Le squat devient confortable : buste plu: The squat becomes comfortable: more upright torso, depth comes cheap. In return, in a hip hinge, a long torso is a long horizontal lever arm: the conventional deadlift costs the lower back more at equal load.
x.Squat sous toutes ses formes, y compris: Squat in all its forms, including front squat and goblet: it is their ground. Lunges, Bulgarians, depth work.
x.sumo, ou départ surélevé, ou trap bar, l: sumo, or raised start, or trap bar; the literature points that way: a higher torso/height ratio goes with better sumo performance
x.Quadriceps au squat libre, sans complexe: Quads with the free squat, without hang-ups. Posterior chain through short-lever exercises (hip thrust, leg curl, set-up back extension) rather than heavy deadlifts.
x.Le pousser au soulevé conventionnel lour: Pushing them into heavy conventional deadlifts because they squat well and we assume they “should” do everything well. It is exactly the movement where their lever works against them.
x.Tibia long : le squat qui ne coûte rien: Long tibia: the squat that costs nothing
x.Hauteur de genou élevée pour l’entrejamb: High knee height for the inseam. On video: knees far forward at the bottom, torso almost upright, no visible effort.
x.Un tibia long autorise le genou à s’avan: A long tibia lets the knee travel further forward at equal depth, which keeps the torso upright and the lever arm on the knee. The load stays on the quads.
x.Squat profond, front squat, squat gobele: Deep squat, front squat, goblet squat, hack. It is the profile that can truly load the quads with the free squat.
x.en revanche, attention à la cheville : u: however, watch the ankle: a knee far forward demands lots of dorsiflexion, and a long tibia amplifies the demand
x.Ne pas gâcher l’avantage : le squat est: Don’t waste the advantage: the squat is here a real quad exercise, not a rigged global one. The hamstrings will need dedicated work: they won’t follow.
x.Ce profil est souvent pris pour « doué »: This profile is often taken for “gifted”. It is simply well proportioned for that movement. Saying so avoids two things: them thinking they are superior, and others thinking they are limited.
x.Faire de son squat le modèle montré aux: Making their squat the model shown to others. A video sent to an athlete with long femurs as “here’s the right technique” produces six months of frustration over unreachable geometry.
x.Bras longs, grande envergure : le tireur: Long arms, big wingspan: the puller
x.En poussée, un bras long allonge l’ampli: In pressing, a long arm lengthens the range and the lever arm to clear: more mechanical work for the same load, and a longer shoulder strain. In pulling, the same length becomes an advantage: more useful range, more time under tension for the back.
x.Tous les tirages : rowing, tirage horizo: All pulls: rows, horizontal pull, vertical pull, pullover. And presses with machine-bounded range: converging press, chest press, where the travel isn’t dictated by their arm.
x.coûteuses (long bras de levier) : privil: costly (long lever arm): favor guided vertical pulls for volume
x.limiter la descente : l’amplitude coûte: limit the descent: the range already costs more than for others, chasing more adds nothing
x.Construire le haut du corps par le dos,: Build the upper body through the back, which is their ground, and treat the chest with machines and flyes where range is set rather than endured.
x.C’est le profil pour lequel Motion Lab a: It is the profile for which Motion Lab brings the most: grip width is set by measuring the real lever arm at three widths, rather than applying a percentage.
x.Lire sa faiblesse au développé comme un: Reading their weakness in the bench as a lack of chest and adding pressing volume. They already do more work than others at equal load: the problem is range, not volume.
x.Bras courts, humérus court : le pousseur: Short arms, short humerus: the presser
x.Amplitude courte, bras de levier court :: Short range, short lever arm: load climbs fast. The downside is symmetrical: less useful range per rep, so less time spent in the long position (the one that matters most for hypertrophy).
x.Poussées lourdes : développé couché, inc: Heavy presses: bench, incline, overhead. And pull-ups, where a short arm is a favorable lever.
x.allonger la course plutôt que charger: lengthen the travel rather than adding load
x.Amplitude avant charge. C’est le seul pr: Range before load. It is the only profile where the load counter misleads: the kilos climb fast, the stimulus doesn’t necessarily follow. The long position has to be sought exercise by exercise.
x.Attention au dos : un bras court raccour: Watch the back: a short arm also shortens the range of pulls. It is often the profile that “doesn’t feel its back”, not for lack of connection, but for lack of travel.
x.Le féliciter sur ses charges et ne jamai: Praising them on their loads and never looking at their range. Two years later, a huge bench and average chest.
x.Charpente étroite : le V à construire: Narrow frame: the V to build
x.Rapport épaules/bassin bas. À distinguer: Low shoulder/pelvis ratio. Absolutely to be told apart from a high waist measurement: the bone ratio doesn’t move with fat.
x.Moins de largeur osseuse au départ. Le V: Less bone width to begin with. The V won’t come from the frame, so it will come from the lateral delt and lat width: two muscles that respond well to volume and suitable resistance profiles.
x.Élévations latérales à haute fréquence,: Lateral raises at high frequency, under several resistance profiles (cable for the long position, dumbbell for the short). Wide-grip pulldowns and pullovers for back width.
x.mais on hiérarchise : le développé milit: but we prioritize: heavy overhead press builds less visual width than three weekly sessions of well-placed raises
x.lever le pied : ils élargissent la taill: ease off: they widen the waist and work against the intended effect
x.Deltoïde latéral en priorité absolue, pu: Lateral delt as absolute priority, then back width, then waist management. In that order.
x.C’est le profil où l’écart entre « mesur: It is the profile where the gap between “measurement” and “photo” is largest: arm girth can stall while the silhouette changes completely. Follow the photo, not just the tape.
x.Confondre charpente étroite et taille ép: Confusing a narrow frame with a thick waist, and putting the athlete in a deficit to “bring out the V” when the bone ratio won’t budge a millimeter.
x.Charpente large, bassin large : la densi: Wide frame, wide pelvis: density first
x.Largeur biacromiale et biiliaque élevées: High biacromial and biiliac width, thick wrist and ankle. Front photo: marked build even without muscle.
x.Avantage visuel d’emblée sur la carrure,: Visual advantage from the start on the shoulders, disadvantage on waist slimness, which is partly bone too. Circumferences will be high at equal muscle mass: the tape flatters, definition deceives.
x.Tout le travail lourd polyarticulaire :: All heavy compound work: the frame supports it well. Density and thickness: heavy rows, presses, squat.
x.la vigilance porte sur le tour de taille: watch the waist: loaded obliques and breathing in presses to monitor if the goal is aesthetic
x.Gestion de l’enveloppe. Sur ce profil, l: Managing the envelope. On this profile, body composition weighs more than exercise choice: one point of body fat shows more.
x.Objectifs de circonférence à recalibrer: Circumference goals to be recalibrated upward: they start higher and progress slower in percentage. The same muscle gain gives a smaller tape difference.
x.Comparer ses tours de bras à ceux d’une: Comparing their arm girth with that of a fine frame and concluding they “gain better”. At equal muscle, they measure more. It isn’t the same thing.
x.Ossature fine : le trompe-l’œil du mètre: Fine bones: the tape’s optical illusion
x.La circonférence mesure os + muscle + gr: Circumference measures bone + muscle + fat. With less bone, more muscle is needed for the same number. In return, definition shows earlier and the physique looks leaner at equal body fat.
x.Rien de particulier mécaniquement. C’est: Nothing special mechanically. It is a programming and expectations profile, not an adjustment one.
x.et le suivi : si le mètre est le seul in: and the tracking: if the tape is the only indicator, the athlete will conclude they aren’t progressing. Cross-check with the photo and the weight lifted.
x.Volume sur les groupes qui portent la si: Volume on the groups that carry the silhouette (delts, back, calves) because for them, proportions create the visual effect, not absolute circumferences.
x.C’est le profil qui abandonne. Il faut l: It is the profile that gives up. It must be given the right measuring tool from the start: waist/arm ratio, photo under constant lighting, workload, and be explained why the centimeter lies to them.
x.Lui parler de « potentiel génétique » ou: Talking to them about “genetic potential” or “FFMI”. A wrist circumference predicts no ceiling: it changes the unit of measurement, not the achievable result. RepCore will never say otherwise.

x.ni la hanche, ni l’épaule, ni la flexion: neither the hip, the shoulder nor the forward bend has been tested

x.L’amplitude manquante se travaille, elle: Missing range of motion is worked on, not bypassed with a variation: load within what is available and lower the bar as it improves.
x.Ossature fine et charpente étroite : sui: Fine bone structure and narrow frame: track the waist-to-arm ratio and the constant-lighting photo rather than circumferences alone. With this profile, arm circumference can stall while the physique changes completely.
x.Avec moins d’os, il faut plus de muscle: With less bone, more muscle is needed for the same tape number: cross-check with the photo and the weight lifted, otherwise the centimeter will suggest a stall that doesn’t exist.
